description.narrative:
This project will work primarily on the Ing River basin. Ing river is a major Mekong tributary in the Upper Mekong Basin of Northern Thailand. The river is 260 kilometres long and covers an area of 7,388 km2, originating in Phayao province and passing through Chiang Rai province before emptying into the Mekong River at Baan Pak Ing, Chiang Khong District. The river is endowed with rich natural resources and ecosystem diversity, including seasonal flooding forests, mountains, rivers, stream tributaries, and twelve sub-watershed areas.
The basin faces many anthropogenic disturbances and climate challenges. Basin-wide temperature as well as change in climate patterns are expected to increase, with an anticipated increase in daily temperatures of 2°C [1]. Large rainfall events (i.e., greater than 100 mm/day) are expected to occur more frequently. This will change the hydrological cycle, impacting both agriculture and fishery sectors [2].
Despite these significant impacts, there is no basin-wide mitigation plan, nor a collaborative platform for climate risk reduction. Furthermore, there is currently no timely and accessible hydrological and meteorological information. Asa result, Early Warning Systems (EWS) in this basin have not been well established. In addition to climate risk, water flow is disrupted due to upstream and downstream hydropower construction and operation. Farmers and fishers are getting lower yields and want toidentify alternatives. In some communities, the cost of pumping water is increasing due to low river levels, placing pressure on strained livelihoods. In other cases, there is increasing community conflict regarding water allocation.
The primary objective of this project is to increase the community resilience of vulnerablegroups who face challenges due to changes in water flow (quantity, timing, quality) resulting from climate change and dam construction in the Mekong River basin. The proposed research has two phases. In the first phase (year 1-2), we aim to have a greaterunderstanding of trends, impacts, and community profile i.e., hydrological-meteorological and land use trends, their level of water security, their traditional knowledge and their level of dependency of aquaticresources. The second phase (year 3) aims todisseminate the results and co-generate local and national mitigation plans by further engaging with communities and policy makers. A research consortium combining both academics from various fields (hydrology, fishery,ecological economics, and socialanthropology) and local community members will address the research question (i.e., how to improve the community resilience?) from different perspectives. The consortia are led by Mae Fah Luang University (MFU).

participating-org.narrative:
Mae Fah Luang University (MFU) was established as an autonomous public university, under the Royal Charter, in 1998, with generous support from the Royal Thai Government. The University was established to meet the needs of people in the north of Thailand, and to commemorate the gracious contributions of the King's Mother, Her Royal Highness Princess Srinagarindra, lovingly known to her subjects as "Mae Fah Luang." From its inaugural class of 64 students in 1998, MFU has become Thailand's fastest growing post-secondary institution with an enrollment of just under 15,000 students. After little over a decade of operation, MFU is already well known for its high-quality teaching, research, and service to the people of the north, as well as Thailand.
Mae Fah Luang Unviersity's campus consists of a large complex of modern, state-of-the-art buildings, spanning more than 800 hectares. The campus is located in a spectacular setting of mountains and trees, an environment conducive to teaching and learning in a clean, inviting setting. As both a regional and national university, MFU provides high-quality education services and resources for the neighboring countries of the Greater Mekhong Sub-region (GMS), and reaches out to all of Southeast Asia.
Philosophy MFU follows the aspiration of Her Royal Highness Princess Srinagarindra to "restore forests and develop people", and striving to "developing people; cultivating knowledge; instillingquality; upholding virtues; and conserving the environment".
Vision A Leading University in ASEAN with International Recognition
Mission To produce quality human resources and develop excellence in academics, research, and innovations for the society under disruptions to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals in accordance with Thailand’s development.
